_comment: Decidr Weekly Marketing Report — Week 26 (22–28 Jun 2026). HubSpot funnel/product/channel/geo/SQL pulled live 2026-07-06. Meta/LinkedIn/Google spend from Supermetrics (AUD). Website/GA4 + creative galleries flagged placeholder.

highlight.html: Strong week — DecidrOS pipeline and a first closed-won deal. 244 new contacts (193 subscribers + 51 on the qualified track), with 38 MQL+ (75% of qualified), 10 SQL+, 5 opportunities and 1 closed-won (james kelder · DecidrOS, via the Mercha case study). DecidrOS drove the quality — 22 MQL+ and 6 SQL+. The Facebook "AI Roadmap" demo campaign converted 9/9 to MQL and produced 2 opportunities (James Fletcher, Cameron Abbott) plus 3 SQLs; Google's AI Roadmap PMax added another DecidrOS SQL (Julian Grant).

observations.html: Strongest qualified week in the series. 51 ex-subscriber contacts, 38 MQL+ (75% of qualified), 10 SQL+, 5 opportunities and 1 closed-won — a clear step up from the surrounding weeks.

DecidrOS pipeline + first closed-won. DecidrOS drove 22 MQL+ (65% of ex-sub) and 6 SQL+, including james kelder converting to customer via the Mercha case study. The DecidrOS funnel is both deep and converting.

"AI Roadmap" FB demo: 9/9 MQL, 2 opps + 3 SQLs. Every demo lead qualified, producing opportunities (James Fletcher, Cameron Abbott) and SQLs (Richard Negri, Rana Sharif, Jim Skiadas) for $2,256 — $251 / MQL. The clearest scale candidate.

Google PMax delivered a qualified lead. "Decidr AI Roadmap PMax" ($241) produced a DecidrOS SQL (Julian Grant) — Google's first HubSpot-attributed qualified contact in weeks. Worth watching whether PMax can repeat it.

Events drove volume, little qualification. Women in Tech (38 contacts, 3% MQL, $3,160) and AI Readiness AU/SG/USA (79 contacts, ~1% MQL) generated top-of-funnel volume but few near-term MQLs — expected for event/awareness, but watch cost per qualified lead.

4 of 6 opps are sales-created (Unassigned). Dita Kuksal, Sabrina Chow, Jeff Mowry entered via CRM; only Cameron Abbott + James Fletcher (and won deal kelder) are marketing-attributed. Tagging product/source on manual opps would sharpen attribution.

Paid media $14,466 — Meta $11,440 (79%), LinkedIn $1,595, Google $1,431. Blended $90 / paid lead. Meta carried volume + quality; LinkedIn ran mostly awareness (0 MQL); Google is small but now contributing SQLs.
